title: Independent insurance agency or marketing organization (life insurance, annuities, mortgage protection, agent recruiting)
basis: Recalled general knowledge, 2026-10-23; hosts not re-fetched (UNVERIFIED). Insurance is YMYL and heavily regulated, so the pack leans on trade associations, local partners that refer clients (lenders, real-estate agents, estate-planning attorneys, CPAs) and trust profiles, and away from paid rankings and lead networks.

domainTypes.note: National Association of Insurance and Financial Advisors; local chapters list members and sponsor events
Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America (the 'Big I') and its state affiliates, for independent agencies
trade news site; check its contributor and press-release terms before sending anything (UNVERIFIED)
reviews the client can read; follow its review rules and the FTC endorsement rules
company page and licensed-producer profiles; also the main recruiting channel; put the website link and the licence number in the profile

patterns.why: an insurance agents' association or chapter
a quote-comparison or agent-finder site (most are lead sellers: vet before use)
a service a homeowner or retiree also needs (lender, real-estate agent, estate-planning attorney, CPA, financial planner): a referral partner

angles: Fill in every field of the professional profiles that matter (association chapter, carrier agent-locator pages, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn) with one identical agency name, phone, state licence number, NPN and website link.

Publish carrier-neutral explainers (mortgage protection vs PMI, fixed vs fixed indexed annuity, term vs permanent life) with a named author, a licensed reviewer and a last-reviewed date; local news sites, lender and CPA resource pages and AI answers cite pages like these.

Build a referral-partner page of real partners (mortgage lenders and loan officers, real-estate agents, estate-planning attorneys, CPAs, financial planners) and ask each to list the agency back; confirm with compliance that no referral payment breaks the state's rules on commissions and inducements.

Host a plain-words workshop (first-time home buyer protection, retirement income basics) at a library, credit union or chamber with no product pitch; get it on the chamber, library and city event calendars.

For recruiting: publish an honest 'how agents are paid' page (commission-based, independent contractor, licensing steps and costs, no income figures) and ask community-college business departments, workforce centres and industry association career pages to list it.
Sponsor a youth team, school fundraiser or neighbourhood event; ask for the sponsor-page link.
avoid: Paying a 'Top Insurance Agent' or 'Best Annuity Agent' list that sells the ranking without labelling it advertising.
Buying links on insurance-quote blogs or lead-generation networks, or from sites that dress paid placement as independent reviews.

Reviews written by staff, paid for, or collected only from happy clients (FTC Endorsement Guides, 16 CFR Part 255); also breaks the insurance advertising rules on testimonials (UNVERIFIED section, see rules/industries/insurance-agency.json).
Guest posts or partner pages that carry guaranteed-return, risk-free or tax-free-retirement claims: the agency answers for the claims it supplies (see INS-GUAR-001 and INS-TAX-001).
Directories that scrape licence data and charge to 'claim' a profile without checking the licence.
